children: London cocoa futures turned lower on Tuesday after climbing to a one-year peak earlier in the session, while sugar prices rose more than 3%.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled down £42, or 0.9%, to £4,817  per metric ton after setting a one-year high of £4,988 earlier in the session.

* Dealers said a strengthening El Nino weather event could contribute to a fall in production in top grower Ivory Coast, although there may still be a global surplus in 2026/27 — albeit much smaller than in the previous season.

* Rains were below average last week in most of Ivory Coast's cocoa-growing regions, farmers said on Monday, warning persistent dry weather could damage and shorten the September-to-February main crop.
* New York cocoa
fell 3% to $6,571 a ton.

* Ivory Coast has maintained the fixed farmgate price paid to cocoa farmers at 1,200 CFA francs (around $2.12) per kg for the 2026/27 main crop season, agriculture minister Bruno Kone said on Tuesday.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
settled up 0.55 cent, or 3.1%, at 18.36 cents per lb, heading toward the 16-month high hit last week.
* Dealers said tight supplies and strong domestic prices in top consumer India were helping support prices.
* India reduced sugar stock holding limits for dealers to 2,000 quintals from 4,000 quintals earlier, effective from September 15 until November 30, the government said in a statement on Tuesday.
* Citi raised its price target for raw sugar futures to 19 cents per pound in three months and 22 cents per pound in 12 months, saying supply risks continue to build in several producing regions.
* White sugar
gained 3.8% to $534.00 a ton.
COFFEE
* Robusta coffee
settled down $68, or 1.9%, at $3,461 a ton, after setting a 2-1/2-month low of $3,405 earlier in the session.
* Dealers said the robusta market currently had ample supplies, with exports from top producer Vietnam running ahead of last year's pace.
* Robusta certified stocks on ICE were rising, they noted.
* "Shipments of Brazilian conilon (robusta) to Belgium surged in July, heralding a fresh wave of robusta gradings, only partially visible at the moment," said Rabobank.
* Arabica coffee
fell 0.7% to $3.0945 per lb.
* Citi shifted to a neutral-bearish view on coffee, estimating prices for arabica at $3 per pound in three months and $2.75/lb in 12 months.
